name: Defense Health Agency
description: Primary federal buyer of health IT for the Military Health System. Total IT budget: ~$11B annually across COMP accounts.
current_read: DHA is mid-deployment on MHS GENESIS with 13 MTF go-lives scheduled Q3-Q4 FY2026 and 26 additional sites in FY2027. Congress withheld 30% of FY2026 EHRM funding (~$1.02B) pending three conditions due June 1, 2026. The Oracle subcontractor and support ecosystem is the primary addressable market. Digital health and enterprise imaging are the growth areas.

at_risk: EHRM funding (30% withheld pending June 1 conditions)

key_offices: PEO DHMS (Program Executive Office, Defense Healthcare Management Systems)
upcoming_signals: Enterprise Imaging expansion RFP (expected Q4 FY2026)

name: Department of Veterans Affairs
description: Largest integrated healthcare system in the US. VA serves 9+ million enrolled veterans across 1,298 healthcare facilities.
current_read: VA is executing the CCN Next Gen procurement (proposals due April 17, 2026) and managing the ongoing EHRM modernization with Oracle Health. The FY2027 budget request maintains community care funding at $56.2B. T4NG2 is the primary IT services vehicle and is approaching re-compete. The VA ambient AI scribe IDIQ is the largest clinical AI procurement in federal health.
key_offices: VA OIT (Office of Information and Technology)
upcoming_signals: CCN Next Gen proposals due April 17, 2026
VA ambient scribe IDIQ task orders (ongoing)

name: Department of Health and Human Services
description: Parent agency for CMS, ONC, NIH, CDC, and FDA. Oversees the broadest health IT policy portfolio in the federal government.
current_read: HHS is driving data modernization across sub-agencies with a focus on interoperability enforcement. The FY2027 budget proposes targeted AI governance frameworks. HIPAA modernization is under active policy review. HHS IT procurement increasingly flows through CMS and ONC rather than departmental-level vehicles.
key_offices: OCIO (Office of the Chief Information Officer)

name: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT
description: Sets health IT interoperability standards, certifies EHR technology, and enforces information blocking rules. Small office with outsized regulatory impact.
current_read: ONC is enforcing TEFCA and expanding USCDI requirements. Information blocking enforcement actions are increasing. The USCDI v4 standard is in development. ONC procurement is limited but its regulatory decisions shape billions in private-sector and government health IT spending.

at_risk: ONC budget is small and vulnerable to broader HHS cuts

name: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health
description: Newest federal health research agency (est. 2022). Uses OTA and other flexible procurement to fund breakthrough health technology.
current_read: ARPA-H is executing its first wave of major programs: ADVOCATE (agentic clinical AI), Sprint for Women's Health, and health security resilience. Awards for ADVOCATE TA1/TA2/TA3 are expected June 2026. ARPA-H uses OTA procurement extensively, making it accessible to non-traditional vendors. FY2027 budget status is uncertain given broader HHS review.

budget.fy2027_request: Zeroed in proposed budget (executing FY2026 funds)
at_risk: FY2027 budget zeroed in HHS proposal — executing on existing appropriations

name: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
description: Administers Medicare, Medicaid, ACA marketplaces, and CHIP. Largest single payer in the US healthcare system.
current_read: CMS is executing the ClaimsCore RFP (the largest claims processing modernization in CMS history) and advancing data modernization across its systems. AI fraud detection and payment integrity are growth areas. CMS procurement is large-scale and long-cycle, with multi-year IDIQs as the dominant vehicle type.
key_offices: CCIIO (Center for Consumer Information and Insurance Oversight)
OAGM (Office of Acquisition and Grants Management)
